title: Lift a ball too big to grip onto its stand, cradled on two battens held one in each gripper
instruction: Put the blue ball in the brass holder on top of the stand. It is too big to grip: hold one batten in each gripper, bring the battens against the ball low down from front and back, and lift it on the two together.
context: Some loads are too big to grip and too round to squeeze: a ball, a melon or a glass globe rolls out of a pinch. Two straight bars brought against it low down from opposite sides make a cradle, the way two spatulas lift a cake. Each hand holds one bar, the bars must rise and move together, and the load must be carried across them, not along them, or it rolls off.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. A blue ball, 15 cm across (wider than a gripper opens, 9.4 cm) and 150 g (a hollow plastic ball), rests on the table 33 cm forward on the centre line. Two square wooden battens, 40 cm long and 2 x 2 cm thick, 80 g, lie on the table running left to right, centred on the centre line, one 24.5 cm forward (in front of the ball) and one 41.5 cm forward (behind it). A stand, nearer the arms: a fixed dark grey block 4 cm front to back, 6 cm wide and 6 cm tall, centred 20 cm forward and 6.2 cm left of the centre line, with a fixed brass holder on top, a frame 6 mm tall round a slot 2.4 cm wide (front to back) and 4 cm long (left to right) that the ball sits in. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead and wrist videos and with a ruler. 1.0: the ball rests in the holder's slot (its centre within 1 cm of the slot's centre line front to back and within 2 cm of the slot's middle left to right, its lowest point from 1 cm below to 5 mm above the holder's top), still for 2 s. 0.5: at some point the ball is lifted with its lowest point more than 5 mm above the holder's top (7.1 cm above the table), but it does not end resting in the holder. 0.0: anything else.
reset_notes: Put the ball back on its mark and lay the battens back at their marks; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the ball is a rigid sphere, the battens rigid square bars and the stand fixed blocks. Loose objects get rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Dream-1 sees the 320 x 176 frames it expects; the demo video is rendered at 1280 x 720.
